newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH CABINET DELAYS INCOME, EXCISE TAX VOTES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH CABINET DELAYS INCOME, EXCISE TAX VOTES.

text.p: The Czech cabinet agreed on Wednesday to pull decisions on changes to income and excise taxes from the agenda of its session which was still in progress well into the evening, a government spokesman said.

Spokesman Ivo Strejcek said decisions on changes in the tax code on personal and corporate income tax and excise taxes on alcohol, tobacco and petrol, would be delayed until the government had more information on which to base its decisions.
Earlier the cabinet agreed to raise the value added tax on electricity and natural gas to 22 percent from five percent beginning in 1998. The measure must be approved by parliament.

The cabinet had planned to discuss a reworking of the tax code with proposals to alter corporate income tax brackets and raise excise taxes, but instead continued its closed-door debate on a proposal to raise state-controlled rents by an average of 50 percent from July 1.
Private TV Nova reported on Tuesday that the Finance Ministry would propose to cut corporate tax next year to 35 percent from 39 percent and to widen income brackets for personal income tax.
The ministry has declined comment on the report.
